HELD TO RANSOM - RANSOMWARE AND THE CITY

By: Joy Summers | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The shadow kill hackers almost brought the city of Johannesburg to a standstill. How can you protect your data from malicious cyber criminals

Unique Selling Point:
THE CITY OF JOHANNESBURG AND A BUSINESS OWNER AGREE TO SPEAK ABOUT THEIR EXPERIENCES OF RANSOMWARE ON THE RECORD

Summary:
Ever heard of the Shadow Kill hackers? The Best 777 or Sun Pixel? They are all the names of Cyber criminals who take over computers, encrypt your data and demand a ransom normally in Bitcoins to unlock your data. Don’t pay and you could find your information out on the web for all to see and criminals to use.

In October the City of Johannesburg was hit by the shadow Kill hackers who demanded R500 000 in Bitcoins to unencrypt the data of the entire city. This was their ransom note:

“All your servers and data have been hacked. We have dozens of back doors inside your city. We have control of everything in your city.”

The city came to a standstill but they say they did not pay, millions of users data was not compromised, and that international experts had worked around the clock to restore the situation.

According to the latest report from Europol, Ransomware maintains its reign as the most widespread and financially damaging form of cyber- attack. Hundreds of businesses around South Africa quietly pay and move on, learn the lesson and keep their back up data off a server far away from the vulnerabilities of the internet.


Further information:
The Shadow kill hackers didn’t just target the city. Cape Based Club Leisure group also got hit and their refusal to pay ended up costing them dearly. Below is a copy of the note that shadow kill posted on the website - - click on the links and it gave out company passwords and all the salaries from the CEO down.

21-10-19 :::: Hello all from Shadow Killers,
Club Leisure / First Group SA by Stuart Lamont in South Africa has been compromised very hard !!! We have managed to get inside their internal network with Domain Admin access to all folders, files, emails, systems. EVERYTHING!!!
They don't have phone lines anymore, so emails, no services... LOL check their facebook post as they LIE TO CUSTOMERS AND DONT TELL THEM THE TRUTH!!! https://www.facebook.com/FirstGroupManagementSA/
"Dear Guests,
Please note our telephone lines are currently down.
We apologise for the inconvenience and hope to get our phone line up and running as soon as possible.
Please keep a look out for further updates on our social media pages.
Your patience is greatly appreciated."

******* ALL ARE DOWN ! *******
https://www.clubleisure.co.za
https://www.firstgroup-sa.co.za
https://www.clubtech.co.za
******* ALL ARE DOWN ! *******

WE HAVE BEEN IN THEIR INTERNAL NETWORK AND DOWNLOADED ALL SENSITIVE DATA. YOU CAN DOWNLOAD IT ON THE LINKS BELOW.

EMAIL PASSWORDS (including CEO):

Some sensitive data including passwords and finance data:

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Expect for MORE DATA LEAK :)

shadowkill@tuatnota.com

So who are these malicious cyber criminals? According to cyber expert Jacques Van Heerden they can be anyone who can hire ransom ware off the dark web for 299 USD and make a deal to split the profits of their bounty 70/ 30 with the developers of the ransomware.

Few companies will admit that their data has been compromised. But we spoke to the CEO and the company’s IT manager about their experience. Let’s call the company R2D2.
In May this year the IT guy “Frans” turned on his computer and soon realized what had happened. Sun pixel wanted five bitcoins for every server they had encrypted and the company had between 15 and 20 servers. So began the negotiation and eventually Dan got the hacker down to R70 rand. They got their data back and began backing it up. But this was not the end of the story. Since then they have been attacked by ransom ware hackers another 3 times- the last one only two weeks ago. They don’t negotiate and have upped their cyber security dramatically but each time their data is encrypted the company goes down for a day and they have to begin the laborious process of backing up all the data.

And it’s not just the city and a few random businesses. Its important institutions like the Civil aviation authority. They too were held to ransom in July, but the CEO told Carte Blanche they didn’t lose important information regarding air safety. But that they are still backing up some of their data. Pilots who insist on anonymity have told Carte Blanche that they know that this is not the case as they have had to give the CAA data that they should have already had.

Carte Blanche speaks to the CITY OF JOHANNESBURG, THE CAA CEO, business owners, IT managers and experts to find out how prevalent is the crime, what damage can be done and how to protect the data of your business from these malicious cyber- criminals.

Press Release:


Your money or your Data – the Rise of Ransomware
Global foreign exchange network Travelex is reeling from the fallout of having to shut down its websites across 30 countries to contain a cyber-attack on New Year's Eve, in which hackers demanded a ransom of US$6 million to delete sensitive stolen client information – dates of birth and credit card information. But South African companies and institutions are not immune to the epidemic of ransomware attacks, as the City of Johannesburg found out late in 2019. So how can you protect your business, and what can your organisation learn from those already held to ransom by cyber criminals?
Producer: Joy Summers | Presenter: Derek Watts


Script:


A RANSOM IN CYBERSPACE TX 12th January 2020

Commentary One
Midway through 2019, City power was held to ransom by cyber criminals. It’s data had been encrypted and hackers demanded four dollars a file to release it. That attack brought the utility to a standstill, but what saved City power, was its back up files

Then on Thursday 24th October last year, the city of Johannesburg staff opened their computers to find this note:

All your servers and data have been hacked. We have dozens of back doors inside your city. We have control of everything in your city. We also compromised all passwords and sensitive data such as finance and personal population information.

LINK
Now that’s not a note any of us want to see when we turn on our computers. It’s called ransom ware, pay up or risk losing all your data, and it was posted on the City of Johannesburg’s computers recently

Commentary Two
Group chief technology officer, Cyril Baloyi, was about to write an exam in Pretoria, when one of his IT staff, phoned him, and read out the message from the Shadow Kill hackers. He read us the demand

Cyril
If you don’t pay on time we will upload the whole data available to anyone on the internet. If you pay on time we will destroy all the data we have and we will send your IT a full report about how we hacked your system and security holes. Contact us for more information at Shadowkill@tutanot.com have a nice weekend
Derek
Have a nice weekend, after that?!
Cyril
Yes!

Commentary Three
In 2019 South Africa was the target of four major cyber-attack campaigns within a space of three months. One of those targets was the Civil Aviation Authority.

Pilots approached Carte Blanche anonymously, and told us that the CAA had lost vital data such as licenses for pilots and aircraft. So we put those allegations to CEO, Poppy Khoza at a press conference

Poppy Khoza
We had an incident in July, but I can indicate to you that information through our business continuity plans and the back- up that we have, we did not lose the amount of information that you mentioned. We are still recovering some of the information from our back- ups and that takes a while because we keep data from 1998 to date

Commentary Four
South Africa is unprepared for a major cyber- attack says specialist Craig Rosewarne

Craig Rosewarne
We have got three laws now that are there to assist with dealing with cyber- attacks, and because these laws have not been fully implemented, really its, every man for himself at the moment

Commentary five
Fortunately, Cyril Baloyi who has spent 20 years as a back-up engineer in the private sector had a great team, who came to the aid of the city

Cyril
within an hour and a half there were more than 30 to 40 people here in my office.
I had Semantic, I had Dimension Data, I had Cisco, I had Microsoft here
Derek
At that stage how much control did they have of the city’s data?
Cyril
They did not have much control of the city data they had control of the domain controller password, which means that by that time they had started running their script to try get into each and every machine, to see if they can collect data from that machine. They did not have data!

Commentary six
But with the city under siege he was forced to make a difficult decision

Cyril
Then I said the best thing we can do is shut down the internet

Commentary seven
South Africa has the highest probability in the world of suffering a data breach according to a new report released by IBM and the Poneman institute. Sheldon Hand is IBM’s cyber security executive

Sheldon
What we are seeing is cybercriminals actually holding organisations to ransom by threatening to completely destroy their entire IT infrastructure
Derek
Any indications as to the time to discover a breach and the time to fix it
Sheldon
In a lot of these scenario’s its taking more than 175 days to actually detect that you have incurred a data breach and then another more than 50 days to actually clean it up

Commentary eight
And criminals even hire ransom ware off the dark web says ethical Hacker Jacques Van Heerden

Jacques
Recoil, they guarantee you its small, its fast and undetectable and you don’t need to write the code – they write it for you. It’s a business model

Craig Rosewarne
You know you can pinpoint places like Russia, Eastern Europe, Asia that is really where the brains of the operation sit where the software gets developed, where the platforms that are offered actually reside. One particular group actually made two billion USD, and they have now closed their platform down, basically saying we are going to have a nice, rest of our lives

Commentary nine
The city brought in the Hawks and the attack is now a criminal case.

Derek
What did you learn about the shadow kill hackers?
Cyril
They are not very strong hackers because with that golden key they could have done a lot of things. If I was them hacking the system I would have gone straight to look at the systems direct not looking at peoples machines because you can only get documents sitting on peoples machines

Commentary ten
The Shadow kill hackers had demanded a modest ransom from the city of 4.0 bitcoins.

Derek
Now the possibility of paying must have been right there on the table?
Cyril
When we started yes - On the Thursday night that possibility was there, but remember we were given 3 – 4 days, so our plan is let’s not communicate to these people until we understand what hit us, and then we said no we are not paying these people

Commentary eleven
But the hackers don’t just target big business and cities. Ransom attacks can devastate small companies. This is the CEO and his IT manager of a medium sized business. They have asked us to hide their identity and hope their story can serve as a warning. A story that began in May 2019, when IT manager Frans, tried to log on.

Frans
Well I tried to log in to the systems, got an error saying you entered the incorrect password. I thought fat fingers, tried another user name, gave me the same error.

Commentary Twelve
On the server, he found this message. Hello this is full encryption. Contact Sun pixel2



Derek
Then you knew
Frans
Then I knew it was ransomware, yes

Commentary 13
All the companies master boot files were encrypted. Not even emails worked. If they wanted their data back, only the payment of five bitcoins at a value of around R600 000 would give them the key to unlock their files

Derek
To me it’s such a dark evil business where it’s impossible to get to grips with the enemy?
Frans
You are basically dealing with a terrorist

Commentary 14
The company had backed up their data, but it was on the same network, and hacker Sun Pixel two, had their back ups under lock and key as well. CEO Garth

Garth
There were back up servers, but the infiltration was right through from top to bottom

LINK
They were in a delicate predicament, pay up and maybe get their data back. Refuse to pay and go out of business.

Garth
We ultimately decided to say ok we will pay um because that is the only way we can get out of this

Commentary 15
But paying is not something our ethical hacker recommends

Jacques
You never pay the ransom. If you pay the ransom they will come back

Commentary 16
Often, he says the hackers create back doors

Jacques
A hacker when he accesses your network he will create a back door. He will plant it on such a fashion that you will back up that back door for weeks on end before he strikes you. So now when he strikes you, you think it’s fine I am going to restore my data, when you restore your data you just restored his back door into your network



Commentary 17
Some hackers are so brazen, they have a help line for ransom payments, but Frans was given a secure email address where he negotiated the ransom down from R600 000 to R60 000

Frans
At the end we got down to 0.5 bitcoins
Derek
How long did it take?
Frans
The initial attack was the middle of May, and we finished negotiating and got the keys at the end of May, and then the work really started, to get the data
Derek
so the work isn’t over once you have paid
Frans
No, then it actually starts

Commentary 18
But within weeks, they were hit again, this time by a different hacker- Best 777. They refused to pay, but BEST 777 just kept on trying.

Frans
We had four attacks this year in the space of seven months. Number two, three and four where from the same guys.

Commentary 19
All told they lost about 3 months of productivity, as a result of the attacks.

GARTH
It’s like running to war without a rifle, those bullets are going to hit you. So you are sitting there you helpless. We have survived the whole action, the whole ordeal – we can carry on with the business, but we are much more aware

Commentary 20
You need layers of security says Craig Rosewarne starting with up to date anti- malware
Craig: The first step is prevention, the second thing is awareness, if you people don’t click on the necessary attachments that they shouldn’t you can stop problem in its tracks, failing that you need a sound back up plan. We use a three-point plan- you need to have at least three files backed up – two external storage devices and one remote cloud based solution
Derek
Have you calculated what this attack has cost the city?
Cyril
The attack has cost the city plus minus R50 million. I have a report on my desk that says that the day we were hit we were sitting at 24% now sitting at 98 % protection.
Derek: Have you found out where the vulnerabilities was and how they actually invaded?
CYRIL Yes we do have the time we have the mac address of the machine we believe is the one that invaded our system. We also have the country where we believe this IP address was connecting from
Commentary 21: It took the city two weeks to recover and Baloyi and his team virtually slept at their offices. He says this time they were lucky, but he is concerned that IT security, must be taken more seriously by government
Cyril
This matter has already been briefed to the president. What we raised with them is that we don’t think the country is ready to deal with such so there must be a team that is formed to deal with these issues

THE END
PROMO ONE
Last year the City of Johannesburg was hit by a ransom ware attack. They were not alone, cyber criminals are attacking local companies and encrypting their data unless they pay up.
PROMO TWO: In 2019 Cyber criminals held the city of Johannesburg to ransom and said they had control of everything in the city
Cyril Then I said the best thing we can do is shut down the internet
PROMO THREE : What does a company do when it gets a ransom note to say its data has been encrypted and the only way to get it back, is to pay a ransom in bitcoins to a faceless cyber -criminal?

Derek Now the possibility of paying must have been right there on the table? Cyril When we started yes - On the Thursday night that possibility was there, but remember we were given 3 – 4 days, so our plan is let’s not communicate to these people until we understand what hit us, and then we said no we are not paying these people Commentary eleven But the hackers don’t just target big business and cities. Ransom attacks can devastate small companies. This is the CEO and his IT manager of a medium sized business. They have asked us to hide their identity and hope their story can serve as a warning. A story that began in May 2019, when IT manager Frans, tried to log on. Frans Well I tried to log in to the systems, got an error saying you entered the incorrect password. I thought fat fingers, tried another user name, gave me the same error. Commentary Twelve On the server, he found this message. Hello this is full encryption. Contact Sun pixel2 Derek Then you knew Frans Then I knew it was ransomware, yes Commentary 13 All the companies master boot files were encrypted. Not even emails worked. If they wanted their data back, only the payment of five bitcoins at a value of around R600 000 would give them the key to unlock their files Derek To me it’s such a dark evil business where it’s impossible to get to grips with the enemy? Frans You are basically dealing with a terrorist Commentary 14 The company had backed up their data, but it was on the same network, and hacker Sun Pixel two, had their back ups under lock and key as well. CEO Garth Garth There were back up servers, but the infiltration was right through from top to bottom LINK They were in a delicate predicament, pay up and maybe get their data back. Refuse to pay and go out of business. Garth We ultimately decided to say ok we will pay um because that is the only way we can get out of this Commentary 15 But paying is not something our ethical hacker recommends Jacques You never pay the ransom. If you pay the ransom they will come back Commentary 16 Often, he says the hackers create back doors Jacques A hacker when he accesses your network he will create a back door. He will plant it on such a fashion that you will back up that back door for weeks on end before he strikes you. So now when he strikes you, you think it’s fine I am going to restore my data, when you restore your data you just restored his back door into your network Commentary 17 Some hackers are so brazen, they have a help line for ransom payments, but Frans was given a secure email address where he negotiated the ransom down from R600 000 to R60 000 Frans At the end we got down to 0.5 bitcoins Derek How long did it take? Frans The initial attack was the middle of May, and we finished negotiating and got the keys at the end of May, and then the work really started, to get the data Derek so the work isn’t over once you have paid Frans No, then it actually starts Commentary 18 But within weeks, they were hit again, this time by a different hacker- Best 777. They refused to pay, but BEST 777 just kept on trying. Frans We had four attacks this year in the space of seven months. Number two, three and four where from the same guys. Commentary 19 All told they lost about 3 months of productivity, as a result of the attacks. GARTH It’s like running to war without a rifle, those bullets are going to hit you. So you are sitting there you helpless. We have survived the whole action, the whole ordeal – we can carry on with the business, but we are much more aware Commentary 20 You need layers of security says Craig Rosewarne starting with up to date anti- malware Craig: The first step is prevention, the second thing is awareness, if you people don’t click on the necessary attachments that they shouldn’t you can stop problem in its tracks, failing that you need a sound back up plan. We use a three-point plan- you need to have at least three files backed up – two external storage devices and one remote cloud based solution Derek Have you calculated what this attack has cost the city? Cyril The attack has cost the city plus minus R50 million. I have a report on my desk that says that the day we were hit we were sitting at 24% now sitting at 98 % protection. Derek: Have you found out where the vulnerabilities was and how they actually invaded? CYRIL Yes we do have the time we have the mac address of the machine we believe is the one that invaded our system. We also have the country where we believe this IP address was connecting from Commentary 21: It took the city two weeks to recover and Baloyi and his team virtually slept at their offices. He says this time they were lucky, but he is concerned that IT security, must be taken more seriously by government Cyril This matter has already been briefed to the president. What we raised with them is that we don’t think the country is ready to deal with such so there must be a team that is formed to deal with these issues THE END PROMO ONE Last year the City of Johannesburg was hit by a ransom ware attack. They were not alone, cyber criminals are attacking local companies and encrypting their data unless they pay up. PROMO TWO: In 2019 Cyber criminals held the city of Johannesburg to ransom and said they had control of everything in the city Cyril Then I said the best thing we can do is shut down the internet PROMO THREE : What does a company do when it gets a ransom note to say its data has been encrypted and the only way to get it back, is to pay a ransom in bitcoins to a faceless cyber -criminal? metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): The shadow kill hackers almost brought the city of Johannesburg to a standstill. How can you protect your data from malicious cyber criminals
metadata.Unique Selling Point: THE CITY OF JOHANNESBURG AND A BUSINESS OWNER AGREE TO SPEAK ABOUT THEIR EXPERIENCES OF RANSOMWARE ON THE RECORD
metadata.Summary: Ever heard of the Shadow Kill hackers? The Best 777 or Sun Pixel? They are all the names of Cyber criminals who take over computers, encrypt your data and demand a ransom normally in Bitcoins to unlock your data. Don’t pay and you could find your information out on the web for all to see and criminals to use. In October the City of Johannesburg was hit by the shadow Kill hackers who demanded R500 000 in Bitcoins to unencrypt the data of the entire city. This was their ransom note: “All your servers and data have been hacked. We have dozens of back doors inside your city. We have control of everything in your city.” The city came to a standstill but they say they did not pay, millions of users data was not compromised, and that international experts had worked around the clock to restore the situation. According to the latest report from Europol, Ransomware maintains its reign as the most widespread and financially damaging form of cyber- attack. Hundreds of businesses around South Africa quietly pay and move on, learn the lesson and keep their back up data off a server far away from the vulnerabilities of the internet.
metadata.Further information: The Shadow kill hackers didn’t just target the city. Cape Based Club Leisure group also got hit and their refusal to pay ended up costing them dearly. Below is a copy of the note that shadow kill posted on the website - - click on the links and it gave out company passwords and all the salaries from the CEO down. 21-10-19 :::: Hello all from Shadow Killers, Club Leisure / First Group SA by Stuart Lamont in South Africa has been compromised very hard !!! We have managed to get inside their internal network with Domain Admin access to all folders, files, emails, systems. EVERYTHING!!! They don't have phone lines anymore, so emails, no services... LOL check their facebook post as they LIE TO CUSTOMERS AND DONT TELL THEM THE TRUTH!!! https://www.facebook.com/FirstGroupManagementSA/ "Dear Guests, Please note our telephone lines are currently down. We apologise for the inconvenience and hope to get our phone line up and running as soon as possible. Please keep a look out for further updates on our social media pages. Your patience is greatly appreciated." ******* ALL ARE DOWN ! ******* https://www.clubleisure.co.za https://www.firstgroup-sa.co.za https://www.clubtech.co.za ******* ALL ARE DOWN ! ******* WE HAVE BEEN IN THEIR INTERNAL NETWORK AND DOWNLOADED ALL SENSITIVE DATA. YOU CAN DOWNLOAD IT ON THE LINKS BELOW. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Screenshots Proofs: https://gofile.io/?c=FBhGYp EMAIL PASSWORDS (including CEO): https://gofile.io/?c=kbyn2w Employees salaries: https://gofile.io/?c=FUVwzG Some sensitive data including passwords and finance data: https://gofile.io/?c=GJKdmg ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Expect for MORE DATA LEAK :) shadowkill@tuatnota.com So who are these malicious cyber criminals? According to cyber expert Jacques Van Heerden they can be anyone who can hire ransom ware off the dark web for 299 USD and make a deal to split the profits of their bounty 70/ 30 with the developers of the ransomware. Few companies will admit that their data has been compromised. But we spoke to the CEO and the company’s IT manager about their experience. Let’s call the company R2D2. In May this year the IT guy “Frans” turned on his computer and soon realized what had happened. Sun pixel wanted five bitcoins for every server they had encrypted and the company had between 15 and 20 servers. So began the negotiation and eventually Dan got the hacker down to R70 rand. They got their data back and began backing it up. But this was not the end of the story. Since then they have been attacked by ransom ware hackers another 3 times- the last one only two weeks ago. They don’t negotiate and have upped their cyber security dramatically but each time their data is encrypted the company goes down for a day and they have to begin the laborious process of backing up all the data. And it’s not just the city and a few random businesses. Its important institutions like the Civil aviation authority. They too were held to ransom in July, but the CEO told Carte Blanche they didn’t lose important information regarding air safety. But that they are still backing up some of their data. Pilots who insist on anonymity have told Carte Blanche that they know that this is not the case as they have had to give the CAA data that they should have already had. Carte Blanche speaks to the CITY OF JOHANNESBURG, THE CAA CEO, business owners, IT managers and experts to find out how prevalent is the crime, what damage can be done and how to protect the data of your business from these malicious cyber- criminals.
